title: Vectors in Two Dimensions
seo_title: Grade 11 Physical Sciences: Vectors in Two Dimensions Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 11 Physical Sciences: Vectors in two dimensions
standard_text: The resultant of perpendicular vectors (Pythagoras and trigonometry); resolving a vector into perpendicular components; the resultant of vectors by the tail-to-head and component methods; closed vector diagrams for objects in equilibrium. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 11, Physics: Vectors in two dimensions)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): resultant vectors, perpendicular components, the tail-to-head method and equilibrium. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Resolve vectors into x and y components.
key_sub: The resultant is found with Pythagoras: R² = Rₓ² + R_y².
body_html:
How to think about it

A vector has magnitude and direction. To add vectors, draw them tail-to-head; the resultant goes from the tail of the first to the head of the last. For two perpendicular vectors, the size of the resultant is √(x² + y²) and the angle is found with tan θ = y/x.

Any vector F at an angle θ to the horizontal has components Fₓ = F cos θ and F_y = F sin θ. If an object is in equilibrium, the resultant force is zero and the force vectors form a closed polygon.

Example

3 N east and 4 N north. Resultant?

Pythagoras

Answer: 5 N

Example

20 N at 30° above the horizontal. Horizontal component?

F cos θ

Answer: 17,3 N

Common mistakes

  • Adding vectors at right angles as if they were in a straight line.
  • Using sin for the adjacent component.
  • Forgetting to give the direction of the resultant.

faq.q: When is the resultant of two forces largest?
faq.a: When they act in the same direction.

faq.q: What does a closed vector triangle show?
faq.a: That the three forces are in equilibrium: the resultant is zero.
